title: Session-skein realignment and graceful OOM fallback for cross-environment KV corruption
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + Dedicated + Private) reported sudden GPU OOMs coinciding with persistent KV cache corruption and increased memory fragmentation. The pattern indicates a race between the session allocator, prefix/KV reconciler, and async evict sweeper that leaves session 'skeins' (fragmented KV chains) which prevent reclaim and gradually saturate GPU allocator slabs.

Observed behaviour: On medium to long-running sessions (>30m) with bursty prompt patterns we saw slow growth in pinned KV handles (not freed), rising device memory pressure and then sharp OOM spikes. Corruption signatures include mismatched KV index checksums and tombstones replaying into active session namespaces after compaction. Incidents affected hosted burst pool, several Dedicated customer clusters under high concurrency, and a single on-prem Private deployment where older kernel scheduling exposed the timing window.

Goal: Ship a low-risk runtime patch that (1) ensures safe reclamation of dangling KV handles and breaks skeins before they cascade, (2) adds a graceful OOM fallback that rejects heavy allocations with a deterministic degrade-to-smaller-model path when safe, and (3) deploys canary + phased rollout across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with monitoring and rollback capability.

Scope: Runtime allocator + KV index layer + request router (fallback policy). Excludes long-term redesign of session layout; that's follow-up work. This ticket covers patch, tests, canary rollout, and customer communications/playbook.
comments: 2026-02-25 - Triage: Pager duty alerted on 2026-02-24 22:14 UTC for Hosted burst pool OOM wave. Initial triage (Ava, Liam, Priya) tied symptoms to persistent KV handle growth. Created ticket and notified SRE/Support for customer impact assessment.

2026-02-26 - Data collection: Added enhanced kvcache telemetry to staging: per-session handle_count, reclaimable_bytes, last_reclaim_ts. Observed a reproducible growth pattern using internal repro harness (repro/run-oom-skein.sh).

2026-03-01 - Root cause hypothesis: Race between async_evict sweep and session_compactor where tombstone re-insertion can resurrect handles due to stale iterator state. Leads to non-idempotent compaction and retained pointers into slab arenas -> fragmentation and unfreeable allocations.

2026-03-03 - Mitigation (hot): Deployed config gate to Hosted burst pool: kvcache.async_evict_concurrency=1 and session_compactor.force_full_scan=true. Reduced OOM frequency by ~78% for affected tenants. Communicated mitigation to support and affected customers (AcmeTravel, FinteraPilot).

2026-03-04 - Patch proposal: Implement (a) a lightweight skein-breaker that atomically validates iterator epochs before tombstone replay, (b) a deferred free queue drain tied to GC safe points to ensure slab pointers are not resurrected, and (c) a fallback policy in router: on allocation failure, attempt model-variant downgrade or immediate queued retry with latency-bound rejection. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2489

2026-03-06 - Review: Design review with Ryan (SRE), Mei (PM), and Carlos (Security). Security ok with deferred free approach; requested additional metrics and an opt-in flag for Private on-prem customers. Added kvcache.skein_breaker_enabled flag and exhaustive unit tests.

2026-03-08 - Testing: Unit tests and fuzz harness added. Staging stress run (12h) on p4d-equivalent nodes: zero leaked handles observed across 100k sessions and memory growth curve flattened. Performance overhead measured <1.5% p50 latency for generate requests.

2026-03-09 - Canary plan: 5% of Hosted traffic (burst pool) for 24h, then 25% for 12h, then 100% if stable. Dedicated: manual canary on two customer clusters with opt-in via support. Private: provide patch bundle and coordinate upgrade window; opt-in required. Monitoring: add grafana overlays for reclaimable_bytes, skein_breaker_hits, allocation_retries, fallback_invocations.

2026-03-10 - Canary 5%: Deployed half of canary (control vs variant) and observed: skein_breaker_hits=1200, allocation_retries reduced by 85%, no customer-visible errors. One regression detected in a legacy on-prem kernel path -> paused rollout for that host class and added regression ticket ENG-777778.

2026-03-11 - Rollout: Continued canary to 25%. Documented rollback steps: flip kvcache.skein_breaker_enabled=false and revert router fallback. Communication drafted to support and account teams with customer-facing KB: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/KV+Skein+OOM+Playbook

2026-03-12 - Next steps: Finish Dedicated customer manual upgrades, coordinate Private package for the one affected on-prem customer, and schedule postmortem. Add follow-ups: long-term session-layout redesign (RFC), improved KV-index checksumming, and a chaos test for compactor/evict races. Assign follow-up ENG-777779.

PRs / Artifacts: Runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2489, Staging repro harness https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro/tree/main/oom-skein, Incident notes https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-023
